title: Ice melting on a scale: mass stays the same
subject: Chemistry

sources.title: NGSS 5-PS1-2: Measure and graph quantities to provide evidence that regardless of the type of change that occurs when heating, cooling, or mixing substances, the total weight of matter is conserved
OpenStax Chemistry 2e, 1.2 Phases and Classification of Matter

steps.title: Scales
steps.instruction: Trace both scales and their screens.

note.text: A scale measures how much matter something has. We'll weigh the same jar before and after a change.

steps.title: Jars
steps.instruction: Trace both jars and their lids.

note.text: The lids seal the jars, so nothing can get in or out.

steps.title: Ice cube
steps.instruction: Trace the ice cube in the first jar.

note.text: Before: a solid ice cube in a sealed jar. The scale reads 100 grams.

steps.title: Water
steps.instruction: Draw the top of the water in the second jar.

note.text: After: the ice has melted into liquid water. Its particles moved apart, but none disappeared.
note.remember: Melting changes the state, not the amount.

steps.title: Predict
steps.question: The ice melted in the sealed jar. What will the After scale read?

options.feedback: Yes. When matter changes from solid to liquid, the total amount of matter stays the same.

options.text: Less than 100 g, because water is lighter than ice
options.feedback: The same particles are still in the jar, so the mass is still 100 g.

options.text: More than 100 g, because water takes up the jar
options.feedback: No new matter got in: the jar is sealed. It still reads 100 g.

options.text: 0 g, because the ice is gone
options.feedback: The ice didn't vanish. It turned into water, which still weighs 100 g.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: You take the lid off and leave the jar for a week. Now it weighs less. What happened?

options.text: Some water evaporated: it left as a gas into the air
options.feedback: Right. The water particles weren't destroyed. They escaped into the air as a gas, so the jar holds less.
Matter isn't destroyed. The water evaporated and went into the air as a gas.
The scale is fine. With the lid off, some water evaporated into the air.
The jar is the same. Some water left it as a gas, so there's less matter inside.

steps.title: Fair test
steps.question: Why did we keep the lid on while the ice melted?

options.text: So no matter could get in or out of the jar
options.feedback: Yes. Sealing the jar means any change on the scale would show matter appearing or disappearing. None did.
The lid is there so nothing escapes or gets in, so we can compare fairly.

options.text: To make the ice melt faster
options.feedback: The lid makes the test fair: no matter can escape or get in.
Both jars have a lid, so that's the same. The lid stops matter escaping.
